body.p: There lives an old man, he has five daughters: "Epkalke, the one being after Epkalke, the middle one, the nameless one, and the little one. The old man said: "Epkalke, get water". "No, I'm working". "The one being after Epkalke, bring water". "No, I'm working". "Middle one, bring water". "No, I'm working". "Nameless, bring water". "No, I'm working". "Little one, bring water". "No, I'm working". The old man went to the ice himself, he went for drinking. He began to drink, his beard froze on. "Ice, let me, I'll give my Epkalke". The ice became stronger. "Ice, let me, I'll give the one being after Epkalke". The ice became stronger again. "Ice, let me, I'll give the middle one". The ice became stronger again. "Ice, let me, I'll give the nameless". The ice became stronger again. "Ice, let me, I'll give the little one". The ice let [him]. The old man came home, he said: "Little one, go to the ice, take along your toys". The little one went off, she sat down on the ice, the ice swam downstream, the ice carried away the little one. It was swimming long, she saw a little fire at the shore, she said: "Ice, wait, let me go to the fire to warm myself!" The ice said: "No, no, I have no sleeping place". The little one went to the small fire, there an old woman is living. "Granny", the little one asked, "where does the ice bring me?" The old woman said: "Little one, I don't know at all, maybe the one with two tambourines knows it". The little one went to the ice. Then again a small fire was seen, again she spoke to the ice. "Ice, wait, let me go to the small fire to warm myself". "No, no, I have no sleeping place". The little one went to the small fire. An old woman is living [there]. "Granny, where does the ice bring me?" "Little one, I don't know at all, maybe the one with three tambourines knows it". Like this the little one came to the one with ten tambourines. "Ice, wait, let me go the small fire there to warm myself!" The ice didn't go. The little one went to the old woman, she asked: "Granny, where does the ice bring me?" "Little one, the ice is bringing you to the middle of the world, the ice is deceiving you. Little one, don't look back". The old woman gave [her] two awls. "Little one, you hold yourself to the earth with these ones". The little one was climbing. The ice started singing: "Heladan, Heladan, look around, look down stream, [there is] a stone for grinding dye". "I don't look back, the foreheads of humans seem to be stones". "Heladan, Heladan, look around, look downstream, [there is] a whetstone". "I don't look around, the shins of dead persons seem to be whetstones". "Heladan, Heladan, look around, look downstream, [there is] black dye". "I don't look around, the excrements of dead persons seem to be excrements [= black dye(?)]". "Heladan, Heladan, look around, look downstream, [there is] red lead". "I don't look around, the blood of dead persons looks like red lead". "Heladan, Heladan, look around, look downstream, [there are] leather wrinklers". "I don't look around, the backs of dead persons look like leather wrinklers". "Heladan, Heladan, look around, look downstream, [there are] scrapers [for scraping leather]". "I don't look around, the holes in the pelvic bones of dead persons look like scrapers". "Heladan, Heladan, look around, look downstream, [there are] grindstones". "I don't look around, the ankles of dead persons look like grindstone". "Heladan, Heladan, look around, look downstream, [there are] little bowls". "I don't look around, the skulls of dead people look like bowls". "Heladan, Heladan, look around, look downstream, [there are] flints". "I don't look around, the forearms of dead people look like flints". Heladan went off, she went to the bear. The bear said: "Kill me, flay me, put my heart besides you for sleeping, [put] my kidneys to the holy place in the tent, my duodenum and my rectum opposite, strew my fur in a dry pit, hang my small intestine on a dry, fallen tree, put my head on the holy place in the tent". Heladan killed the bear, she made everything as it had said. In the morning Heladan woke up, she saw: "Opposite to her an old man and an old woman are sleeping, at the holy place two children are playing, behind this place an old man is sleeping, outside reindeer are roaming around. The dry pit is full of reindeer. She went out of the tent, on the fallen tree harnesses are hanging. She selected reindeer, she started measuring the reindeer with her forearm. They don't stand, they are trembling. All bad ones couldn't stand her hand. Heladan found such a small reindeer, that one could stand her forearm. There she harnessed [it], mounted it and rode off. She was riding and riding, she came to singing Evenks. She was running through their tent, the Evenks didn't make it to catch her. She went through ten tents, in the tenth one they caught her. When they caught her, Heladan began to sing: "Why did I go away from the bear's heart, why did I go away from the bear's kidneys, why did I go away from the bear's duodenum, why did I go away from the bear's rectum, why did I go away from the bear's head, why did I go away from the bear's intestines".
